name: Mattaniah
title: Levite and musician in the temple
summary: Mattaniah was a Levite who served in the temple after returning from exile in Babylon. He is mentioned in several contexts in the books of Ezra and Nehemiah, including as one of those who played music at the dedication of Jerusalem's wall, and as one of those who had taken foreign wives and had to send them away. The name means 'gift of the Lord' and was common among Levites and priests during this period.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned among the Levites who took foreign wives
keyEvents.description: Mattaniah was one of the priests who had taken foreign wives during the exile and who had to separate from them in accordance with Ezra's reforms.

keyEvents.title: Served at the temple gate
keyEvents.description: Mattaniah, one of the Levites and firstborn son of Shallum of the Korahites, was in charge of what was baked on griddles for the temple offering.

keyEvents.title: Participation in Ezra's reading of the law
keyEvents.description: Mattaniah stood at Ezra's right hand as he read the law to the people by the Water Gate and witnessed this important event in Israel's spiritual renewal.

keyEvents.title: Musical service in the temple
keyEvents.description: Mattijah was among the Levites appointed to serve with music before the Lord's tabernacle, playing harps and lyres.

keyEvents.title: Service at the Wall Dedication
keyEvents.description: Mattijah participated in the celebration and musical performance during the dedication of Jerusalem's rebuilt wall under Nehemiah's leadership.
